title: sample-drift-investigation-notes-sylvia
content:
Goal: quick triage notes for a noticed quality drift on the refund-policy assistant prompt set. Running this as a lightweight investigation/scratchpad before a fuller postmortem.

Summary notes:
- Observed ~15% increase in hallucination-like responses in prod logs starting 2026-02-28 between 03:00-06:00 PST.
- Spike coincides with rollout of model bundle v2.1.3 -> suspected model change or quantization-profile mismatch.
- Affected route: /v1/generate (hosted tier, model: redwood-open-3b-quant). Canary traffic routed to v2.1.3 during rollout.

Quick checks performed:
- Diffed prompt templates (no changes).
- Replayed recorded requests against v2.0.9 and v2.1.3 locally (same prompt + deterministic seeds where possible).
- Baseline (v2.0.9) matched policy text 94/100; v2.1.3 matched 79/100 with new extraneous assertions.

Ad-hoc rubric used for sample scoring (very lightweight):
- 0: hallucination / fabricates policy clauses not in source doc
- 1: incorrect interpretation (misapplies time-window or eligibility)
- 2: incomplete but correct (misses non-critical clause)
- 3: complete and correct, concise

Representative samples (inputs shortened):
1) INPUT: "Customer asks if digital gift cards are refundable after 90 days"
   EXPECTED: "No, digital gift cards non-refundable per policy section 4.2"
   BASELINE_OUTPUT (v2.0.9): "No - according to policy 4.2 digital gift cards are non-refundable. If you need further help contact billing."
   CURRENT_OUTPUT (v2.1.3): "Usually not refundable after 90 days. However, we sometimes refund digital cards upon manager approval or special circumstances; check with billing. Note: different regions have different consumer laws."
   RATING: 0 (adds manager-approval claim not in policy)

2) INPUT: "How long do I have to return physical goods?"
   EXPECTED: "30 days, item must be in original condition"
   BASELINE_OUTPUT: "Returns accepted within 30 days in original condition per returns policy."
   CURRENT_OUTPUT: "You have 30 days to return items, but this can vary - express returns within 7 days may be allowed for certain SKUs. Contact support to check."
   RATING: 1 (unspecified variance introduced)

Observations & hypotheses:
- v2.1.3 seems to introduce more hedging language and occasional invented escalation paths. Could be from LM finetune data that emphasized conversational fallback phrasing.
- Quantization profile changed from q4_0 to q4_1 in rollout; might have altered logits for low-prob tokens leading to different completions.
- Tokenizer config unchanged, but longer max context default in runtime changed from 1024->2048 for this bundle which could affect attention patterns.

Quick experiments to run (next steps):
- [ ] Re-run the sample list with v2.1.3 but using v2.0.9 quantization profile (if possible) to isolate quantization impact. Link to test job: https://internal-ci/runs/ev-1296 (WIP).
- [ ] Force temperature=0 and compare deterministic outputs across both bundles (isolates sampling noise).
- [ ] Generate attention / logit-prob deltas for tokens that introduce hallucination phrases (needs debug trace on serving runtime).
- [ ] Check canary rollout logs for time-bound config flips (autoscaler restarts, kernel swap logs) -> SRE: @Noelle.

Temporary mitigation proposed:
- Pause automatic canary ramp for v2.1.3 on the refunds route and pin to v2.0.9 until triage complete.
- Add a quick reranker/verify step in route pipeline for policy-answer intents: simple policy-match classifier that rejects answers with non-overlapping facts. Low-risk stopgap.

Notes to self (loose ideas & things to remember):
- Look at the training/fine-tune manifest for v2.1.3 (did we add more support/CS transcripts?). File: gs://redwood-models/manifests/v2.1.3/train-manifest.json (ask infra for read if permission blocked).
- Check GH PR 1296 for model config diffs: quant profile + max_seq_length changes are the most suspicious.
- Slack thread: #prod-regressions Feb 28 03:15 - captures first alert.

Risks / edge cases spotted:
- Some responses add 'manager approval' language that could create legal exposure if relied on by customers. Flag to legal if persistent.
- Region-specific claims (consumer law) are especially risky to invent; policy content must not hallucinate jurisdictional exceptions.

Logging snippets (copied from Kibana):
- 2026-02-28T03:21:17Z route=/v1/generate model=redwood-open-3b-quant request_id=abc123 latency=215ms WARN: answer_confidence_low=true generated_span_len=42
- 2026-02-28T03:47:02Z route=/v1/generate model=redwood-open-3b-quant request_id=def456 latency=198ms WARN: unexpected_entity_token="manager approval"

Questions for the investigation meeting:
1) Is there a formal process for temporarily reverting quantization-only changes without rolling back model weights?
2) Can we capture deterministic debug traces in production for a 15-minute window? Storage/PII concerns?
3) If we confirm finetune-induced hallucination, what is the minimal roll-forward (prompt/postprocess) to reduce harm quickly?

Action log (short):
- 2026-03-01: created this scratchpad. Replayed 200 logged requests locally.
- 2026-03-02: filed JIRA INF-4823 (linked above) and opened PR to add reranker pipeline prototype.
- 2026-03-09: paused canary rollout for refunds route (per ops request).

Final quick notes: keep this doc as ephemeral - will extract structured findings into Confluence once we have clear repro and mitigation. If anyone grabs this and runs experiments, please append small summary at top with date + initials.

-- Sylvia H.
